xocs:funding-text.$: This paper presents the results of a shake-table test on a superstructure model supported by a prestressed high-strength concrete (PHC) pipe pile in soft soil. The primary objective is to investigate the dynamic response of the PHC pipe pile in soft soil influenced by soil–structure interaction (SSI). Accordingly, a single PHC pipe pile with iron blocks is constructed and embedded in soft soil. First, the production of the physical model of the PHC pipe pile and experimental details are elucidated. Then, the study focuses on the dynamic response of the soil–pile–superstructure system considering different ground motion types and peak ground accelerations (PGAs). Finally, the inertial and kinematic effects on the dynamic response of the PHC pipe pile are analyzed. The results show that the SSI effect can increase the predominant period of the superstructure. With the SSI effect, the seismic design should consider the adverse effects of long-period and pulse-type ground motions on the pile. The SSI effect caused the rate of increase in the pile bending moment to be gradually higher than the increase in PGA. Moreover, the dynamic response of the PHC pipe pile is mainly dominated by the inertial effect.To examine the dynamic response of a PHC pipe pile in soft soils under the influence of SSI, this study conducts a shake-table test on a PHC pipe pile supporting a superstructure in soft soils. The fabrication method of the physical model of the PHC pipe pile and the tests conducted are presented in detail in this paper. The results of typical tests on the soil and superstructure under different ground motion types and PGAs (including boundary effect, acceleration, and response spectra) are interpreted. Based on the dynamic response of the soil and superstructure, the dynamic response of the PHC pipe pile in soft soils under the influence of SSI is discussed in the paper in terms of acceleration, deflection, rotation, stiffness degradation, strain, bending moment, and shear force. Finally, the inertial and kinematic effects on the dynamic response of the PHC pipe pile are highlighted.

The research described is funded by the Science and Technology Innovation 2025 Major Project of Ningbo, China (Grant No. 2019B10076) and the Zhejiang Province Natural Science Foundation, China (Grant No. LY23E080001).
